judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short audit right with a defined notice period; 'including but not limited to' precedes a list but the subject (payments) is already general.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement limits audit scope or record retention, so there is no competing provision to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All obligations, burdens and requirements set forth hereunder or otherwise associated with the lands covered hereby' is a boundless catch-all whose reach beyond the Agreement is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the specific duties in Sections 8, 11 and 15(B) and could be read to import unstated lease obligations, though nothing directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As nearly as possible to its original condition' and an unqualified duty to 'settle surface damages' are soft standards, though familiar ones.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 5(B)'s restoration and reclamation duty and 8(A)'s surface restoration indemnity without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, concrete access right expressly at Farmor's sole risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Exhibit C's witnessing rights and 8(A)'s allocation of risk to Farmee for its own operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated anti-transfer list ending in 'or subjected to a lien or liens', clear on its face if broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17 makes the Agreement binding on 'successors and assigns' and Exhibit D expressly contemplates Assignee assignments on notice down to a 25% working interest, so the absolute consent requirement needs reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dated reporting duty with defined content; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Exhibit C's production reporting and Exhibit D's monthly royalty statements, but adds rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is labelled a 'Right of First Refusal' but operates as a preferential offer/option with no third-party offer to match, and it terminates on several overlapping conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conditions the right on Farmee drilling and completing the test well 'on or before August 31, 1996, as described in Section 3(A)', yet 3(A) requires only commencement of drilling by that date and completion within 45 days of total depth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall run with said Farmout Lands' is a real-covenant assertion in a clause headed 'Execution', and the effectiveness sentence is boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Binding 'successors and assigns' pulls against 15(D)'s flat bar on assignment without consent, and 'effective as of the date first above written' answers the preamble's 'effective as hereinafter provided'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short numbered checklist of deliverables with a stated copy count; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C addresses duties to 'Operator', a term never defined in the Agreement (which speaks of Farmee), leaving the obligor identified only by implication.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'EREX' is used for a party never so defined, and 'qualified wellsite geologist', 'thoroughly and timely' and 'properly and timely analyzed' are unmeasured standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(D) makes assignment contingent on compliance with 'all geologic requirements as set out in Exhibit C', so these soft standards become conditions of earning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Significant indications', 'adequately tested' and 'good oilfield practices' are all judgment standards with no benchmark in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Through 3(D) these become preconditions to the assignment of Operating Rights, giving the vagueness real operative bite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Routine daily prepaid report' appears to be an error for 'prepared' (or 'prepaid' telegram), and daily written confirmation of a Monday-Friday telephone report is odd but intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 10(A)'s routing of well data through Exhibit C and with B.3(b)'s immediate notice duty for non-routine events.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Non-routine occurrences such as ...' is an open-ended illustrative list, and 'significant shows' has no threshold.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Farmor's designated representative' is not identified in 10(B) or Exhibit C D.1, which name different individuals, so the recipient of immediate calls is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite copy-count duty triggered when the Operator receives the documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C C.1 requires 'one copy' of overlapping items while flagging 'THREE COPIES', so the copy requirements across the exhibit are not uniform.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survey list carries unmarked or stray check marks and a blank 'Other', so which logs are actually required cannot be read off the page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Compliance with Exhibit C is a condition to earning under 3(D), which makes an unfilled checklist consequential.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Timely notice' is undefined with no lead time specified, leaving the notice period at large.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: B.3(b) requires immediate telephone notice of intent to core, test or log, so the two provisions state the same duty to different standards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'One copy of the following (unless otherwise specified)' is immediately followed by 'Two final prints' and a 'THREE COPIES' heading, and item (e) is an open catch-all for 'any other data pertinent'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against B.3(c)'s two-copy rule for the same categories of reports, leaving the required number inconsistent within the exhibit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full information on the completion progress' is a broad standard sitting in front of an enumerated list, the general/specific tension in miniature.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements 15(E)'s annual production report and 10(A)'s confidentiality period without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'And other similar data' extends an enumerated list, but the clause is a delivery instruction of little contestable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address and attention party differ from the Farmor notice block in 10(B) (different street line, 'Mike Stamper' rather than 'Lester Zitkus'), so proper delivery could be disputed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A form preamble with blanks for the date; nothing ambiguous in the identification of the parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Farmout Agreement preamble and Exhibit D's closing reference to the same unrecorded agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The granting language leaves the well number and the size of the 'acre circle' blank, so the extent of the grant is not ascertainable from the instrument itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanks are meant to be filled from 2(D)'s 80-acre (gas) and 40-acre (oil) circles, but 3(E)'s depth limit and Exhibit D's deeper-strata reservation must also be layered on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So long as oil and gas or either of them is produced in paying quantities' plus a shut-in alternative is a familiar habendum formula, but 'paying quantities' is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'paying quantities' where 2(H) defines shut-in wells by 'commercial quantities', and its perpetual term must be squared with Section 13's termination of the Farmout Agreement and 4.A's survival of royalties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A comprehensive, conventionally drafted disclaimer and indemnity; broad but not uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 9's no-warranty term and Section 8(A)'s indemnity, so the instrument is consistent on this point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient' is an elastic measure of which easements pass, though the subjection to the underlying leases is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 9's disclaimer of title warranty and with 15(B)'s requirement that Farmee obtain surface-owner permission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The percentage and the substance produced are left blank, and 'gross proceeds received by Assignee ... without deductions of any kind, except ... severance tax' is exactly the phrase royalty disputes turn on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.A reserves the same royalty on gross proceeds 'without deductions of any kind' with no severance-tax carve-out, and says nothing of the lien or the monthly 28th-day payment date created here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Grants, conveys and assigns other such rights ... only to the extent set forth herein' is awkwardly worded ('other such rights' has no antecedent).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with 2(D)'s 'that portion and only that portion' limitation and with the deeper-strata reservation, so the reservation theme is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice of intent to assign, a 25% working-interest floor and a consent requirement for operator transfers are specific, though 'in any other manner assign its rights, duties or obligations as operator' is a broad catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15(D) of the Farmout Agreement bars any assignment by Farmee without prior written consent, which cannot easily coexist with a regime permitting assignment on mere notice down to 25%.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formation below which everything is reserved is left blank, so the vertical boundary of the reservation is unascertainable from the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2(F) and 3(E) set the vertical limit by depth (4,000 feet / 100 feet below total depth), a different metric from the unnamed formation used here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate binding successors and assigns; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside 15(D)'s consent bar and Exhibit D's own assignment restrictions, which qualify who the assigns can be.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence subordination of the assignment to the Farmout Agreement, with only the date left blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Farmout Agreement controlling, which helps rather than hurts the 4.A / Exhibit D royalty mismatch, though it does not say which text prevails on conflict.
